blocks.heading: Shop steward
blocks.text: A shop steward is an unpaid representative of a trade union at business level, elected by union members at a specific workplace. The role connects workplace members with union representation and management. Unpaid refers to the representative role in this syllabus description; it does not mean the person has no ordinary paid job. A paid full-time union officer based elsewhere is not automatically the workplace’s shop steward. Identify the workplace election and representative role, not simply someone who knows about unions.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: At fictional Kena Meals, union members elect an employee to represent their local concerns without additional pay for that representative role. That employee is the shop steward in the stated arrangement. A manager chosen by the employer would not meet the same member-elected description.

blocks.heading: Keeping the ideas apart
blocks.text:
Explain which person fits the syllabus shop-steward role: a fictional paid regional union officer, or an unpaid workplace representative elected by that workplace’s union members.

The elected unpaid workplace representative fits the shop-steward definition. A regional union officer may support workers but does not fit this particular role merely by being a union official. Unpaid concerns the representative role, not the absence of an ordinary job wage.
